PACK.name: Package
PACK.note: UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/PACK. A PACK record is four sections: a header, the Public Package Data (a list of ANAM activities and their values, then a list of UNAM activity ids), optionally the Procedure Tree (only in template packages), the Procedure Data (UNAM/BNAM/PNAM triples), and always the Begin/End/Change actions. The same signature means different things in different sections: ANAM opens a public activity or a tree branch, and UNAM is an activity id in the public data and a section marker in the procedure data. [observed: 5,961 PACK records in Skyrim.esm; the public activity's ANAM value names the type of the field that follows it, so the block's layout is chosen by the opener's value].

ANAM.name: Activity Type
ANAM.note: The name of the activity's type, and in the procedure tree the kind of branch. The field that follows holds that type's value, so the same signature means different things depending on this string. [observed in Skyrim.esm: Bool 33,485, Float 5,644, Location 6,838, SingleRef 2,253, TargetSelector 1,578, ObjectList 1,343, Int 1,209, Procedure 878, Topic 354, Stacked 194, Sequence 162, Simultaneous 117, Random 8]

ANAM.name: List Entry Type
ANAM.note: The type of the list's next entry, for example Bool or Int. The entry's value follows.

CNAM.name: Object List Value
CNAM.note: The list's first value. UESP lists this as a float-typed CNAM; in the shipped data it is 4 bytes.

ANAM.name: Branch Type
ANAM.note: The kind of branch: Procedure is the only non-branch element; Random, Sequence, Simultaneous and Stacked are top-level branches that hold procedures. The fields that follow differ from the public activity's.

CIS1.name: Variable Name
CIS1.note: The auxiliary data for the CTDA, replacing its first argument. A variable name rather than a value.

CIS2.name: Variable Name
CIS2.note: The auxiliary data for the CTDA, replacing its second argument.

CITC.name: Condition Count
CITC.note: How many CTDA conditions this branch has. Zero means there are none.

CTDA.name: Conditions
CTDA.note: The conditions under which this branch is active. The package's own conditions are the CTDA in the header.

FNAM.name: Success Completes Package
FNAM.note: A flag: 0x01 means success completes the package.

PKC2.name: Activity ID
PKC2.note: An activity id in this branch. The same id may appear in more than one branch.

PNAM.name: Procedure Type
PNAM.note: The procedure's type, a string. This is a different PNAM from the one in the procedure data section, which is a uint32 flag.

PDTO.name: Topic Value
PDTO.note: The topic the activity uses. A DIAL formid, or a four-character subtype string.

TPIC.name: Topic Reference
TPIC.note: The DIAL record, used for exactly one of the Topic activities in a PACK.

INAM.name: Idle
INAM.note: The IDLE record. Always present, but zero when there is no idle action.

PDTO.name: Topic
PDTO.note: The topic. Always present, and entirely zero when there is no topic. The same struct as the public data's topic value.

POBA.name: On Begin
POBA.note: Marks the start of the On Begin actions. Zero-length.

POCA.name: On Change
POCA.note: Marks the start of the On Change actions. Zero-length.

POEA.name: On End
POEA.note: Marks the start of the On End actions. Zero-length.

TNAM.name: Unknown
TNAM.note: Seen only on one PACK record in the shipped data, and always zero.

BNAM.name: Activity Name
BNAM.note: The activity's name as shown in the CK.

PNAM.name: Unknown
PNAM.note: A flag. Only the values 0 and 1 occur. This PNAM is a uint32, unlike the procedure tree's PNAM, which is a string.

UNAM.name: Activity ID
UNAM.note: The activity id, as a byte. It matches an activity id in the public data; the extra ids are for activities that were deleted from the package and are no longer in the CK.

CIS1.name: Variable Name
CIS1.note: The auxiliary data for the CTDA, replacing its first argument.

CIS2.name: Variable Name
CIS2.note: The auxiliary data for the CTDA, replacing its second argument.

CTDA.name: Conditions
CTDA.note: The conditions under which the package can be active. The procedure tree's CTDA is the same struct, but is specific to its branch.

IDLA.name: Idle
IDLA.note: The idle's formid. There is one per IDLC.

IDLF.name: Idle Flags
IDLF.note: 0x01 = Run In Sequence (otherwise random), 0x04 = Do Once, 0x08 = unknown.

PKCU.name: Package Control
PKCU.note: The package's control struct: flags, the template package, and more flags.

PKDT.name: Package Flags
PKDT.note: The package's flags, type, speed and interrupt behaviour.

PSDT.name: Unknown
PSDT.note: A 12-byte struct whose meaning is not documented.

QNAM.name: Owner Quest
QNAM.note: The package's owning quest. Appears once in the header, and again in the begin/end/change section with a different meaning.

XNAM.name: Unknown
XNAM.note: A signed byte ranging from -77 to 99. There is always one, at the end of the public package data section.

struct.name: value
struct.note: A DIAL formid when the type is Dialogue; otherwise a four-character string such as "HELO" for the Hello subtype.

struct.name: unknown
struct.note: Possibly flags. The values range from 1 to 34.

struct.name: package_template
struct.note: The PACK record used as a template. Only a record whose package type is Package Template may be used, and only in a record whose type is Package.

struct.name: unknown2
struct.note: Possibly flags. The values range from 0 to 29.

struct.name: misc_flags
struct.note: Only the flags with a visible effect in the CK are listed. Many others are set in the game data and are probably holdovers from Oblivion.

struct.name: package_type
struct.note: Only the first bit is relevant: set means Package Template, clear means Package. The value 0x12 is always set, so the byte is usually 0x12.

struct.name: interrupt_override
struct.note: Only the values 0 (None) and 4 (Combat) are observed.

struct.name: preferred_speed
struct.note: Only relevant when the Preferred Speed flag (0x2000) is set.

struct.name: type
struct.note: What kind of location this is.

struct.name: location
struct.note: The location. A formid for Near Reference, In Cell and Near Linked Reference; an alias id for Alias (Reference); a formid for Alias (Location); unused otherwise.

struct.name: type
struct.note: What kind of target this is.

struct.name: target
struct.note: The target: a formid for Specific Reference, Object ID and Linked Reference; a lookup value for Object Type (11 = Weapons: Any); an alias id for Ref Alias; unused for Self.

struct.name: count
struct.note: Always 0 in the shipped Skyrim records.
